title: Dhul Hijjah at home
hookLine: many who plan to sacrifice don't cut hair or nails in the first ten (Muslim)

lines: THE NEW MOON OF DHUL HIJJAH.
cards: The new moon of Dhul Hijjah is sighted. Far away, the pilgrims are in Makkah in their white cloth. And in an ordinary house, a pair of nail clippers goes into a drawer and stays there.
A haircut gets moved to later in the month. Nobody here is on hajj. So why is someone at home suddenly not cutting their nails?
It goes back to one hadith, and to a question anyone who stays behind might ask: how do I take part in a journey I'm not on?

teach.b: Umm Salamah, a wife of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, reports his words in Sahih Muslim, in paraphrase: when the ten days begin, and one of you intends to offer a sacrifice, let him leave his hair and his skin alone.
A small holding back, for someone planning the sacrifice of the coming Eid. Schools of law differ on how binding it is: some treat it as required, some as recommended, and some don't require it.

teach.h: AN ECHO OF THE PILGRIM'S IHRAM.
teach.b: Why it matters: pilgrims in ihram have their own list of things they leave alone, and cutting hair and nails is on it. Some scholars point out the echo. At home, a person keeps one small piece of what the pilgrim keeps.

teach.h: NO DEEDS DEARER THAN IN THESE DAYS.
teach.b: In al-Bukhari, Ibn 'Abbas reports the Prophet saying, in paraphrase, that no good deeds are dearer to Allah than those done in these ten days. They asked: not even striving in Allah's path?
Not even that, he said, except a person who goes out with himself and his wealth and comes back with nothing. Days for everyone, not only travelers.
And a sound you might hear: al-Bukhari mentions that Ibn 'Umar and Abu Hurayrah would go out to the market in these days saying Allahu akbar, and people said it with them.

teach.h: TAKBIR IN THE MARKET, A FAST AT HOME.
teach.b: On the day of 'Arafah, when the pilgrims stand on the plain, some at home fast. Sahih Muslim reports the Prophet's hope that this fast wipes away the sins of the year before it and the year after.

how: In the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah, Muslims at home often increase prayer, charity and takbir, and some fast on the day of 'Arafah; those who intend to offer a sacrifice for Eid al-Adha often leave their hair and nails uncut until it is done, following a hadith in Sahih Muslim.

games.q: what does “dhul hijjah at home” mean?
o: the month of fasting before the Eid feast
the day pilgrims stand on the plain
the pilgrimage month, kept by those at home

games.q: Dhul Hijjah at home — tap the pairs.
p: no deeds dearer than in these ten days
a fast for those at home

s: leaving hair and nails uncut is only for people on hajj

every school of law treats the restraint the same way

not even striving in Allah's path, except one who goes out and comes back with nothing.

games.q: the ten days of Dhul Hijjah have begun. you're not on hajj, but you plan to offer a sacrifice at Eid. what does the hadith in Sahih Muslim ask of you?
o: fast every one of the ten days.
leave your hair and nails uncut.
travel to the nearest mosque each night.
games.why: Umm Salamah reports it: let him leave his hair and his skin alone. a small restraint that echoes the pilgrim's.

practice: Choose one tiny thing to leave alone for a while: hitting snooze, a purchase you don't need, a comment you'd usually make.

Each time you notice yourself not doing it, let that moment point to someone far away who is keeping much more. If you pray, remember the pilgrims each time; if not, notice the space the small restraint opens up.

wordCard.voice: Dhul Hijjah at home. The month of the pilgrimage, kept by those who stay behind: a small restraint, good deeds in the ten days, takbir, and the fast of 'Arafah. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the name of the month of the hajj.

carryVoice: Your line: home, but with them. A small restraint, and a thought sent far away. Eid al-Adha is next.
